summary.text: A 68-year-old married patient with hypertension, taking valsartan, and no reported personal or family cancer history, had a cerebrovascular accident in 2018. Involuntary movements of hemichorea began within weeks, with thrashing motions, left hand twisting and writhing, spastic gait, turning and rolling, and spread to the back and legs. The pre-surgical AIMS score was 12. Major depressive disorder was diagnosed later.

MRI showed an old CVA. Tetrabenazine and amantadine did not respond; haloperidol with diphenhydramine controlled the movements, which returned in 2022 with neck and jaw movements. Olanzapine, memantine, quetiapine, tetrabenazine and amantadine did not respond; aripiprazole and gabapentin gave a relative response. Hyperglycemia, hypoglycemia, Sjögren syndrome, multiple sclerosis and lupus were excluded by laboratory tests and surgery was scheduled.

Under local anesthesia without intubation, a stereotactic frame was applied and MR images obtained. The target was chosen right of the midline; after micro recording, radiofrequency thermocoagulation at 84 °C for 60 seconds produced a right pallidotomy in May 2022. No adverse events or complications were reported, and the result was described as perfect. Post-operative CT showed the lesion in the right GP internus.

The patient was followed for 12 months with neurological examinations at 1, 3, 6 and 12 months. The AIMS score was 2, reflecting significant improvement, and she was treated successfully. Follow-up beyond one year was not possible because she moved to another city.
